### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 85 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ebecfa080db61d27bee06ac2876d69613c29e921` — the merge of head `5b16eb349b8d570ea22c453f279e62ae6e94db7d` into base `50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ebecfa080db61d27bee06ac2876d69613c29e921 && git checkout ebecfa080db61d27bee06ac2876d69613c29e921
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 5b16eb349b8d570ea22c453f279e62ae6e94db7d && git checkout -B drift-repro 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 && git merge --no-ff 5b16eb349b8d570ea22c453f279e62ae6e94db7d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cli/src/utils/flow-undeclared-cycle.ts (`findFlowCycleRefusals`, `FlowCycleRefusalRow`), packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts (step 3a-vii), packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts (step 3b-iii-quater), packages/cli/src/utils/flow-undeclared-cycle.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-flow-region-shape.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts (the `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` row), packages/cli/vitest.config.ts (the `@objectstack/metadata-core/testing` alias) + packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle.ts (`findUndeclaredFlowCycle`, `undeclaredFlowCycleMessage`), packages/metadata-core/src/flow-cycle-corpus.ts and testing.ts (`FLOW_CYCLE_CORPUS`), packages/metadata-core/package.json (`exports` `.` and `./testing`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts (`detectCycles`) and flow-definitions.ts (`canonicalizeFlow`: `applyConversionsToFlow`, `FlowSchema.parse`, `detectCycles`, `validateControlFlow`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts (`findFlowCycleGaps`, `FLOW_UNDECLARED_CYCLE`), packages/lint/src/validate-flow-region-shape.ts (`validateFlowRegionShape`), packages/lint/package.json (dependency edges), packages/cli/package.json (`dependencies`, `exports`), packages/cli/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts (`artifactPackages`), packages/cli/src/utils/extension-field-suffix.ts (the sibling walk's subject rule), the retired packages/cli/src/utils/flow-region-shape.ts at the parent of #29495's merge (the row shape this walk keeps), packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`flows: z.array(FlowSchema)` and `assembledPackageBodyShape`), scripts/check-test-source-alias.mjs (`KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS`, the `@objectstack/cli` entry), .changeset/config.json (the `fixed` group), .changeset/29051-cli-flow-undeclared-cycle.md (read for ②), the precedent changesets 29025-flow-undeclared-cycle-publish.md, 28893-flow-region-shape-at-validate-build.md, 29049-flow-region-shape-lint-rule.md and 29233-flow-region-shape-publish.md as landed on `main`, the card body of #29051, the claim 6580677546 and its amendment 6584349353, the dev report 6587816439, the director ruling 6580265584 on #29025, and the seat order delta for #29051.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line-initial on the PR body and the changeset; no path under `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path: `check-governed-merges --pr 29595` answers 0 of 8 paths hit, 13 surfaces governing). Merge-base `03797bd796477d8603339c79994ccd9a63f7f9b4`; net diff 8 files, 272 insertions, 0 deletions (272 changed lines, under 3,000). The PR file list equals the dev report's `files_changed` and equals amendment 6584349353's declared surface (the new walk, one step each in validate.ts and compile.ts, its tests, the changeset) plus the two deviations the report declares (the parity ledger row, the vitest alias). Nothing under `packages/metadata-protocol/**`, `packages/spec/**`, `packages/lint/**` or `ui/**` moves. `main` has moved 27 commits since the merge-base; the two that touch any cited file are #29526 (the lint registry row, `0814b892`) and #29499 (`3557366c`, spec), neither on validate.ts, compile.ts, the judge, the engine or the corpus. Every non-prose path of the diff is in scope above.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept-set change is at `os validate` and `os build` only** (`@objectstack/cli`). A stack carrying a flow whose top-level `nodes`/`edges` graph, once every edge with `type: 'back'` is set aside, still has a cycle now fails both commands with exit 1: one `VALIDATION_ERROR` row per such flow in `errors` under `--json`, a heading naming ADR-0044 and the rows in text, and `os build` writes no `dist/`. `os lint` is unchanged. No other door moves: the runtime publish gate already refuses the same flow since #29226 (`findFlowCycleGaps`, on `main`), the engine's registration is untouched. **Right**, and it is the one accept-set change in the diff.
2. **Same judge as the engine and the gate, no second DFS.** The walk calls `findUndeclaredFlowCycle` from `@objectstack/metadata-core`, the function `detectCycles` (flow-registration-checks.ts) throws from and `findFlowCycleGaps` (runtime-authoring-gate.ts) asks; `git grep` over `packages/cli/src` and `packages/lint/src` at this head finds no other reader of `Flow contains a cycle`, `findUndeclaredFlowCycle` or `detectCycles` apart from the region rule's docblock. The ruling's 「⛔ No copy of the DFS」 holds. **Right**.
3. **Same graph as the engine.** The engine's `canonicalizeFlow` runs `applyConversionsToFlow`, then `FlowSchema.parse`, then `detectCycles(parsed)`. At both CLI doors the ADR-0087 D2 conversion layer runs inside `normalizeStackInput` (validate.ts step 2, compile.ts step 2) before `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse`, and the stack schema parses every flow with `FlowSchema` (`flows: z.array(FlowSchema)` on the stack and, through `assembledPackageBodyShape`, on each `packages[].manifest`). So `result.data` hands the walk the converted, parsed flow, and `FlowSchema.safeParse` on it is a re-parse of the schema's own output; the judge reads `nodes[].id` and `edges[].source/target/type`, which neither parse nor conversion reorders or rewrites (as the #29226 record established for the gate). An absent edge `type` is `'default'` after parse and `!== 'back'` raw, the same answer. The edge alias spellings (`from`/`to`) are refused by the strict stack schema upstream, as `FlowSchema.parse` refuses them at registration, so no graph reaches one judge and not the other. **Right**: the set refused equals the engine's.
4. **Same sentence.** The row's `message` is `Flow 'NAME' would be refused at registration: ` followed by `cycle.message`, which is `undeclaredFlowCycleMessage(path)`, the string `detectCycles` throws, verbatim. The prefix is the one the lint region rule puts before the engine's sentence on all three authoring commands and now at the gate (#29526); the gate's own `flow-undeclared-cycle` finding carries the bare sentence plus a `hint` and locates on the closing edge (`flows[0].edges[N]`), while this row locates at the flow, which is what the card's acceptance and the seat's delta ask for ("located at the flow"). The dev's acceptance note names the edge-vs-flow difference and that `closingEdgeIndex` is available for a later edge-located row. **Right**.
5. **No false refusal of a declared cycle or a legacy shape.** The judge sets aside only `type: 'back'`; the corpus's `cyc_rework_back`, `cyc_self_back`, `cyc_mid_back` (any one back edge on the loop) and `cyc_diamond` (two paths meeting) are `cycle: null`, and the corpus test pins `[]` for each; the door test's CONTROL stack holds exactly those and exits 0 through both commands. A `fault`-typed closing edge is refused, which is the engine's semantics (`cyc_rework_fault`). Legacy shapes are converted before the parse (①.3), so a flow the engine registers after D2 conversion is one this walk judges after the same conversion. A flow `FlowSchema` refuses is skipped (`if (!result.success) return`), which is unreachable at these doors (the stack schema already parsed it) and, were it reachable, is what the region rule reports as "could not be judged" one step earlier (①.7). **Right**.
6. **Package paths.** `artifactPackages(parsed)` gives the `packages[]` entries with their index and `manifest` body; the walk reads each entry's `body.flows` at `packages[K].manifest.flows[N]`, or the stack's own `flows[N]` when it declares no packages. This is the subject rule the retired #28893 walk used (same three lines at the parent of #29495's merge) and the one `findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals` uses, so the top level of an assembled artifact is not walked, as its sibling walks do not walk it. The unit test pins a refused flow in the second entry at `packages[1].manifest.flows[1]` with the top-level flow ignored. **Right**, and consistent with the CLI's other author-time walks.
7. **Order versus the region rule, and no double report.** The rule table runs first at both doors (validate.ts step 3a-i union run and 3a-ii per-package run, compile.ts 3b and 3b-ii), each with an `errors.length > 0` exit under `splitBySeverity`, so a flow `flow-region-shape-invalid` refuses never reaches step 3a-vii / 3b-iii-quater. The engine judges the cycle (`detectCycles`) before the region (`validateControlFlow`), so an author with both faults reads the region first here and the cycle first at registration; the dev declares this in the acceptance notes, the changeset and the walk's docblock, and amendment 6584349353 accepted it. The two judges read disjoint graphs (`validateControlFlow` never reads the top-level edges; `findUndeclaredFlowCycle` never descends into a region), so one fault yields one row, and no other step of either command reports a top-level cycle (①.2). **Right**: no double report.
8. **Both doors wired, as the ledger demands.** `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` closes the roster: a bare identifier either command calls must sit in exactly one ledger. `findFlowCycleRefusals` joins `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` with the reason it is not a registry rule, and the file's own assertions hold that both commands call it. The step sits before the capability preflight on validate and before the dependency-range check and every artifact write on build (`fs.writeFileSync(artifactPath, …)` is at line 1321, the step at 850). **Right**.
9. **No new package dependency edge, and none the ruling forbids.** `packages/cli/package.json` already lists `@objectstack/metadata-core: workspace:*` (line 73, unchanged); `packages/lint/package.json` still depends on `formula`, `sdui-parser` and `spec` only, and no file under `packages/lint/` moves. The ruling's reason for letter A (no `lint → metadata-core` edge "for a check #29051 can add with one call") is honoured: the check is one call in the CLI. **Right**.
10. **Public surface and new names.** `findFlowCycleRefusals` and `FlowCycleRefusalRow` are module exports under `src/utils/`; `@objectstack/cli`'s `exports` map (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, …) and `src/index.ts` (which re-exports commands and nothing from `./utils`) do not reach them, so no package-public name is added. The wire-visible change is the new row in `errors` of `os validate --json` / `os build --json`, shape `{ path, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', flow, message }`, byte-for-byte the retired `FlowRegionRefusalRow` shape of #28893, and one new text heading. No new rule id, no new export, no spec change. **Right**.
11. **The test-only alias.** `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` gains `@objectstack/metadata-core/testing → ../metadata-core/src/testing.ts`, anchored (`^…$`). The bare `@objectstack/metadata-core` specifier was already aliased to source in the same file before this PR (the `#20158` block, `find: /^@objectstack\/metadata-core$/`), which is why `@objectstack/metadata-core` is absent from `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS['@objectstack/cli']`; the new subpath alias follows that precedent so the corpus the tests read is the checkout's, not `dist/testing.js`. `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, where `check:test-source-alias` runs, is `success` on this head. **Right in substance**; the comment above it is wrong in two places (③).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29051-cli-flow-undeclared-cycle.md`: `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, headline `**BREAKING** fix(cli)!:`, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none — …`, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, Before / Now / Unchanged bullets and a remedy paragraph. The PR title is `fix(cli)!:` and its body carries the same two declaration lines line-initial. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` (which carries `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`) are `success` on this head.
- **The kind is `none`, and `patch` follows.** AGENTS.md's kind is "the change to what a metadata author can write". This diff changes no schema, no accepted value and no door of the protocol: `FlowSchema` still accepts the flow, the engine refuses it as before, and the publish gate refuses it since #29226, which declared that narrowing `narrowed` / `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. What moves here is the CLI's author-time verdict, brought into line with the protocol as it already stands on `main`. That is the face #28893 landed (`fix(cli)`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`, BREAKING banner, `adr-0087` marker) and #29049 landed (`none`, `patch`); #29226 and #29526 are the other face, a protocol door (the runtime authoring gate) refusing a body it accepted, and their `minor` is the level the kind `narrowed` takes there. AGENTS.md's own sentence covers this changeset exactly: "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". **Right**; declarations, level, banner and gates agree, and the seat's claim and delta expected these values.
- Only `@objectstack/cli` moves in the diff and it is the one package the changeset bumps. The `fixed` group in `.changeset/config.json` holds `cli` with `metadata-core`, `metadata-protocol` and `lint`, so the group's next version is the highest level among its pending changesets whatever this one says; `patch` here changes nothing shipped.
- One reading the seat should hold in mind rather than act on: if "a value refused" at any door were read as `narrowed`, this would be `minor`, but that reading would re-rate #28893 and #29049 too and would count the same narrowing twice (once at the gate in #29226, once here). I do not recommend it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`, one: should `os lint` also refuse the cycle (A leave lint blind, B add a `lint → metadata-core` edge, C move the judge into a package lint depends on).** My view is **A**, as the dev recommends, for this card and this PR. (1) The director ruling 6580265584 (letter A, maintainer 「同意」) decided this exact question for the gate and gave the reason: the rule does not move into `AUTHORING_RULES` because that "would add a lint → metadata-core dependency edge for a check #29051 can add with one call". B is the edge the ruling declined; taking it on the CLI card would reverse the ruling's reason without a ruling. (2) C is the card's original option (a), a spec export, which the same ruling settled against ("neither (a) nor (b), the metadata-core export", the delta's reading); it is a `domain:spec` package-graph decision and a new card, not a rider here. (3) `os lint` already does not run any `SHARED_NON_REGISTRY_GATES` row (the capability preflight, the override gate, the suffix reservation, the dependency-range check), so a hand-wired gate lint is blind to has precedent on every row of that ledger, and this PR records the reason in the row. (4) Four-axis: no measured pull for the lint face (the card's reach is `os validate` / `os build`, the doors that ship; nobody reported `os lint` passing such a flow); the long-term shape stays the ruled one (one judge in metadata-core, called from each face); the AI-error axis is served where it matters, the build that emits the artifact now refuses; and no new package edge at startup stage. If the seat wants lint parity later, it is one card (B needs a director ruling reversing letter A's reason; C is the spec lane's), measured on pull, not this head.
- **Forced edit `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts`**: within the claim surface ("its tests", amendment 6584349353), and forced by the closed roster: a new bare identifier both commands call fails the file until classified. The row is placed in the right ledger (both doors call it) with a true reason. **Right**.
- **`packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`** is outside the declared surface; the dev reports it as a deviation named by `check:test-source-alias`. Test-only, one anchored subpath alias, the repo's own mechanism for reading a sibling's test corpus from source. Accepted. **Should-fix (prose, no behaviour)**: the comment above the alias says the bare `@objectstack/metadata-core` specifier "is NOT aliased here: it stays in this package's measured ledger entry"; both halves are false on this tree (the bare specifier is aliased to `../metadata-core/src/index.ts` forty lines below, since #20158, and `@objectstack/metadata-core` is not in the cli ledger entry, which is why the gate is green). The same comment names `src/utils/flow-region-shape.test.ts`, a file #29495 deleted; the file is `src/utils/flow-undeclared-cycle.test.ts`. Fold into any later push; not a landing blocker.
- **`Skills-docs:` line**: the arm is `(narrowing)`, so the claim template owes the PR body a line-initial `Skills-docs:` line beside the two declarations. The changeset carries `Skills-docs: none — …` (and its reason is right: `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` lines 168-172 teach that the resubmit edge MUST be typed `'back'` and that an unmarked cycle is rejected; no skill or doc says `os validate` passes such a flow, the only sentence to that effect being the release-owned #29025 changeset's "do not run this check yet", which this PR makes false in the right direction and which no code PR may edit). The PR body does not carry the line. **Should-fix (body edit, no head move)**, as the #29526 record asked.
- **Full dogfood battery on the final head**: the lane rule (standard order §5) owes the battery on the final head for a narrowing. The dev ran it on `a5b8e9bf` (397 files passed, 3 skipped; 3277 tests passed, 28 skipped, VERDICT 0) and `git diff --stat a5b8e9bf 1f72080c` is exactly the 8-line ledger row in `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts`, a test file no dogfood suite imports. I judge the reading carries to the head; naming it so the seat's ACCEPT accepts the deviation on the record rather than by silence. The CI `Dogfood Regression Gate` parent job is `success` and its shard matrix `skipped` on this head (path filter), so CI adds no battery reading of its own.
- **Dev deviations 2 and 4** (the move into the new walk carried by the merge commit `a5b8e9bf` rather than a separate commit; the progress-checklist tool unavailable) are procedural and leave nothing in the tree beyond the 8 files.
- **Out-of-scope finding, `carrier: none · noted, not filed`** (`os lint` does not give this verdict): answered by the A/B/C view above; nothing to file under Prime Directive #10 (no defect, no contract violation, the declared behaviour is enforced where declared).
- **Check-runs on head `1f72080c` at 2026-11-02T20:41Z: 46 runs; 23 `completed/success`, 13 `completed/skipped`, 10 `in_progress`, 0 failed or cancelled.** Of the ten required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI` are `success`; `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI` are `skipped` by their `ui/**` path filter, as expected for a diff with no `ui/**` path; `TypeScript Type Check` (workspace, debt ledger, consumer gates; `source gates` already `success`) and `Test Core` (shards 1-7; shard 8 `success`) are still `in_progress`. Every completed run is `success` or `skipped`. This record judges the tree and the completed conclusions; the all-green landing precondition is the seat's to read again before queueing.
- Governed surface: none; size 272 changed lines; PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, no relay author to name; the branch `claude/project-thread-s4ddhz` is the one claim 6580677546 names.

### ④ Design judgment

- **packages/cli/src/utils/flow-undeclared-cycle.ts** — holds against the card's scenario and the ruling. Pure (reads the parsed stack only; `safeParse`, never `parse`); one call to the shared judge; the engine's sentence verbatim behind the flow's name; the subject rule and row shape of the walk it replaces, so an author who read #28893's rows reads the same shape. The docblock states the order difference, the lint-blindness and its reason, and the schema-refused skip and why it is unreachable, all of which I verified (①.3, ①.7, ①.9). I tried to break it with: the card's `start → push → check → revise → push` with the loop edge untyped (refused, `flows[0]`); the same with `e5` typed `back` (passes); a `fault`-typed closing edge (refused, as the engine); a self-loop, typed and untyped; one back edge in the middle of the loop (passes, the graph minus back edges is acyclic); two loops, one declared (the undeclared one named); a diamond (passes); the refused flow in the second `packages[]` entry beside a passing top-level flow (one row at `packages[1].manifest.flows[1]`, top level not walked); a flow with both a malformed region and an undeclared cycle (refused for the region at the rule-table step, this step never reached); a legacy shape the D2 layer converts (converted before the parse, judged after it, as at registration). In every case the verdict is the engine's or the declared order difference.
- **packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts and compile.ts** — hold: one step each, the exact shape of the neighbouring hand-wired gates (`emitJson` with the command's own failure envelope under `--json`, `printError` plus `printBulletList` with `JSON_FULL_LIST_REMEDY` otherwise, `this.exit(1)`), placed after the rule table and before the build's artifact write. The parity ledger holds both calls.
- **The narrowing itself against the published spec on `main`** (the face's own question): `FlowSchema` on `main` accepts the flow; ADR-0031 ("the engine is DAG-only") and ADR-0044 (an unmarked cycle is refused, the reduced graph must be a DAG) say the engine refuses it, and since #29226 the publish doors refuse it in the same words.
